# dsh-attest-chain
> **If this helps you, please give it a star** — it helps others find it. Thanks!
Signed chain-of-custody for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) sessions.

Headless agents bypass PR gates entirely; chat UIs show what the agent *said*
it did. This plugin re

cords what the agent actually **did**: every watched
tool result (`bash`, `write`, `edit`, `web_fetc

h`, …) appends a hash-chained,
ed25519-signed custody record to a durable JSONL ledger. Tamper with

any line
and the chain breaks; delete the tail and it no longer matches the published
head. Zero LLM
calls in the trust path.

Family: **dsh-read-guard** guards what the agent reads, **dsh-pr-gate** gates
what it writes, **dsh-
attest-chain** proves what it did.
## Why now (checked 2026-10-12)

Nothing in the dsh plugin ecosystem produces tamper-evident records of agent
activity. The nearest n

eighbours inventory plugins (`dsh-harbor`, 24★ — a
read-only list of what's *installed*) or add LLM-

based reviewing. The
in-toto-shaped lane — signed, verifiable, CI-consumable evidence of what an
age

nt session did — is empty. The signing core is vendored from
agent-attest, whose CI gate
can consume
this ledger as session-side evidence.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Verification is pure and offline: replay the ledger, recompute every digest,
check every link and si

gnature. Publish the head digest (or the public key)
anywhere durable — a PR description, a CI varia

ble — and any later comparison
detects tampering or truncation deterministically.

A keypair is generated on first run; the private half never leaves the
machine running the agent. `s

ign: false` runs a digest-only chain if you only
need tamper-evidence against a published head.
## Compared with qiushi-dsh-evidence-audit

The closest sibling in the awesome security category is
qiushi-dsh-evidence-audit —
same idea (hash-

chained local receipts over `tools/result`), deliberately
different trust posture. Pick by what you

receipts over `tools/result`), deliberately
different trust posture. Pick by what you need to prove:
| | dsh-attest-chain | qiushi-dsh-evidence-audit |
| Chain | SHA-256 links **+ ed25519 signature on every record** | SHA-256 links only (explicitly not

signatures) |
| What a record binds | `sha256` of the model-visible content, tool, callId, error fl

ag | hashes of IDs and outcomes; **no digest of the content the model saw** |
| Git binding | extrac

ts **commit SHAs from shell outputs** — the chain ties work to repo history | none |
| Tamper locali
zation | `verifyChain()` returns the **first bad `{seq, reason}`** (broken link vs digest mismatch v

s bad signature) | file-level verdict |
| Consumption | `verifyChain` is an exported API — dsh-trust

-panel runs it live and shows the result in the sidebar | standalone |
| Privacy stance | content di
gests only, never plaintext; keys stay local | hashes-only by design, POSIX 0600 receipts, no key ma
er plaintext; keys stay local | hashes-only by design, POSIX 0600 receipts, no key material at all |

In short: if you want **attribution and repo-history binding** (who signed,
against which commits),

attest-chain; if you want the **minimum footprint**
with zero key material, qiushi. Both are observe

-only and honest about limits —
neither can prove a command ran correctly, or detect a suffix delete

d before
the ledger was first published.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
From npm — no build step, no `allowBuilds` authorization; git installs are equally prebuilt (`lib/`
step, no `allowBuilds` authorization; git installs are equally prebuilt (`lib/` ships in the repo).
## Configure
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Add `.dsh-attest-chain/` to your repository's `.gitignore` — the private key must
never be committed
; the public key is what a verifier checks.
## Compatibility
- **DSH**: verified against the 0.2.x line (source snapshot 0.2.1-alpha.2); installs on any profile

via `dsh plugin add` (prebuilt `lib/`, no build approval).
- **Node**: >= 20 (CI matrix: Node 20/22/

24 on Ubuntu and Windows).
- **Disposable-profile evidence (2026-10-19)**: `dsh plugin --profile <fr
esh> add github:zhengqiuyang/dsh-attest-chain` → installed in 30s; boot shows `[dsh-attest-chain] ac
tive: …`; `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> remove dsh-attest-chain` → dependencies cleared, bundles res
…`; `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> remove dsh-attest-chain` → dependencies cleared, bundles restored.
## Develop
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The canonical-JSON serializer and ed25519 PEM helpers are vendored from the
sibling `agent-attest` c
heckout (`npm run sync`; CI runs `sync --check`).
## Roadmap

- Session-end in-toto statement envelope (full interop with agent-attest CI)
- Per-session ledgers k

eyed by session id
- A `verify` tool card: replay + verdict inside the Web UI
- GitHub check-run bri
dge: head digest posted to the PR
## Kill criteria

If dsh ships first-party signed session records, or a major plugin-adds
attestation natively, this f

reezes at its last working version with a
postmortem here. The signing core stays owned by agent-att

ast working version with a
postmortem here. The signing core stays owned by agent-attest either way.
## Known limitations
- **Single-process append.** The chain continues correctly within one plugin activation; a second ac
tivation appending to the same ledger starts from GENESIS and will read as a broken link. Use one le

dger per activation, or wait for tail-continuation support.
- **`commitSha` is parsed from tool outp

ut text**, not independently verified against the repository.
- **The signing key lives in `keysDir`
** — an attacker with the same file permissions can re-sign a forged chain. The chain proves order a

nd integrity against the key, not authorship by a specific human.
- Records carry tool name, callId,
error flag, and the content digest — not tool arguments or full file states.
